scenario: AITA for telling my fiance we shouldn't get another bird after we lost ours last night? | Me and my fiance had a lovebird named Rosie. She was the sweetest little thing ever. Last night, she had suffered what we believe to be a sudden heart attack, and she passed away; we have literally no idea how it happened as she was very well taken care of, and she was perfectly fine earlier yesterday. Both of us are devastated right now and grieving, especially my fiance as she has been having severe depression the past few weeks, so this doesn't help her at all. We said our goodbyes, and let her Today as i am playing video games, i overhear her making phone calls to pet shops and animal shelters asking for birds they have. She called her aunt to ask for money to get another bird, so i tried to stop her saying "no we shouodn't, its a bad idea right now. We just lost Rosie last night" i was upset because not only did i find that not healthy, but i saw it as immediately replacing something we both loved. She got annoyed with me and told me it would help her feel better and to grieve. We argued back and forth for a bit. My fiance called me an asshole and said i have no say in the matter, which i feel as though i do because i pay the rent and bills in our apartment, money is super tight cause i am the only one working right now, and it would be my money that pays for this bird (we have separate accounts). At the moment, we are both upset and not talking. I never mentioned we should never get a pet ever again, i just said it would be best to wait until we have time to properly mourn, and maybe when our finances improve. I want to be supportive to her cause she's feeling this pain of loss just as much, if not worse than i am, but i feel like i didnt do it right. Am i the asshole in this scenario? Thanks.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was wrong or right in telling my fiancÃ©e that we shouldn't get another bird after losing Rosie last night. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, Rosie was a lovebird that we both loved dearly. She was very well taken care of, and we had no idea why she suddenly passed away. Both of us are devastated, especially my fiancÃ©e, who has been dealing with severe depression for the past few weeks. This loss has made things even harder for her. I was playing video games when I overheard her making phone calls to pet shops and animal shelters, looking for another bird. She even called her aunt to ask for money to get another bird. I tried to stop her, saying, "We shouldn't get another bird right now. It's a bad idea. We just lost Rosie last night." I was upset because I saw this as replacing something we both loved, and I thought it wasn't healthy. She got annoyed with me and told me that getting another bird would help her feel better and that I had no say in the matter. We argued back and forth. She called me an asshole and said I had no say because I pay the rent and bills in our apartment, and money is tight since I'm the only one working right now. It would be my money paying for the bird, and we have separate accounts. At the moment, we're both upset and not talking. I never said we should never get a pet again; I just said it would be best to wait until we have time to properly mourn and maybe when our finances improve. I want to be supportive because she's feeling this pain of loss just as much, if not more than I am, but I feel like I didn't handle it right. So, was I the asshole in this scenario? Let me break this down. On one hand, I was trying to be responsible. We just lost Rosie, and getting another bird so soon might not be the healthiest way to grieve. Plus, financially, it's a strain since I'm the only one working. I was looking out for our financial stability and trying to prevent what I saw as an impulsive decision. On the other hand, my fiancÃ©e is grieving and feeling the loss deeply, especially with her depression. She might have been looking for a way to cope by getting another bird, thinking it would help her feel better. By trying to stop her, I might have come across as unsupportive or insensitive to her feelings. I also need to consider our relationship dynamics. I pay the bills, which gives me some financial control, but does that mean I have the right to dictate what we do with our money, especially when it comes to something like getting another pet? It seems like I was trying to make a decision that affects both of us without considering her emotional state. Maybe I should have approached the situation differently. Instead of outright saying we shouldn't get another bird, I could have expressed my concerns about timing and finances in a more supportive way. I could have suggested waiting a bit and then discussed alternatives or ways to honor Rosie's memory without immediately replacing her. I also need to reflect on how I handled the argument. Calling her an asshole and saying I had no say in the matter probably escalated things. It's important to communicate in a way that shows understanding and empathy, especially during a difficult time. In the end, I want to be supportive of her, but I also need to protect our financial stability and ensure that any decisions we make are thoughtful and not impulsive. Maybe finding a middle ground, like setting a specific time to wait before considering another pet, would have been a better approach. I also need to consider that she might have been feeling neglected or alone in her grief, and getting another bird could have been her way of coping. By dismissing that, I might have made her feel worse. Overall, I think I was partly right in wanting to wait and consider our financial situation, but I was also wrong in how I approached the conversation without considering her emotional needs. It's a delicate balance between being responsible and being supportive, and I might have leaned too heavily on the responsible side without enough empathy.
